metadata.name: 元
metadata.description: cell A1 — the origin cell. the desktop itself is now the `desktop` origin-application (wallpaper, icons, taskbar, state graph); 元 is the base spreadsheet cell the 🧮 Origin launcher restores. a cell whose output renders elsewhere shows its SOURCE here. type a formula in any cell to grow an app. (kept the default `f` parser — 元 is boot substrate, so it must not depend on the infix compiler which ships in the sheet segment.)

cels.f: (dom "div" (style "padding" "1.2rem" "font" ".92rem ui-monospace,monospace" "max-width" "42rem" "line-height" "1.5") (dom "h2" "🧮 origin") "a reactive spreadsheet that is also a desktop. type a formula in any cell to grow an app. the desktop icons launch apps, right-click the background for display settings, and the round 🕸 button opens the live state graph.")

metadata.name: 元.mount
metadata.description: where the sheet view mounts. the host's one knob; null hides it.

metadata.name: 元.editing
metadata.description: key of the cell currently being edited (null = none).

metadata.name: sheet.editing
metadata.description: ASCII mirror of 元.editing (kept in sync by origin.edit/select/key) — the editing cell key a workbook grid formula can reference (infix cel keys are ASCII; the kanji 元.* can't appear in a formula).

metadata.name: sheet.selected
metadata.description: ASCII mirror of 元.selected (kept in sync by origin.select/key) — the selected cell key a workbook grid formula can reference.

metadata.name: 元.draft
metadata.description: the edit input's in-progress text.

metadata.name: sheet.draft
metadata.description: ASCII mirror of 元.draft for DISPLAY — seeded with the selected cell's source on select/edit/commit so a formula bar (sheetbar) can reference it. NOT written on each keystroke (the bar's input writes 元.draft directly), so the bar never re-renders mid-edit.

metadata.name: 元.error
metadata.description: compile/parse error for the cell being edited (null = none); shown under the active editor so a bad formula doesn't fail silently.

metadata.name: 元.selected
metadata.description: key of the currently SELECTED cell (Excel single-click). The cell keeps rendering its VALUE; the formula bar shows this cell's source and edits commit here. null = no selection.

metadata.name: 元.cells
metadata.description: ordered spreadsheet cell keys: 元 (A1) + genesis-created grid cels.

metadata.name: 元.srcs
metadata.description: cell SOURCES parallel to 元.cells — the view shows a cell's source when its value renders elsewhere (a mount).

metadata.name: 元.view
metadata.description: the FRAME-FIRER (gen-2). Its inputMap.vals lists every whitelisted self-mounting frame cel (cellKeys); referencing vals makes them all deps so they fire + paint. Renders nothing itself — 元, =cels grids, docs, the wiki and the desktop chrome each self-mount their own win.<id>.frame. (Was the gen-1 sheetView render loop.)

metadata.name: content
metadata.description: the 元 base sheet as a gen-2 worksheet body: a single-cell editable sheetgrid whose A1 is the bare 元 cel (the readme). Edit A1 to grow an app; =cels makes more worksheet windows.

cels.f: (sheetpane (sheetbar sheet.selected sheet.draft) (sheetgrid "元" (sheetcells "元" 元) (gridopts sheet.editing sheet.selected)))

metadata.name: state
metadata.description: the 元 window state (gen-2). Hidden at boot when the desktop hydrates (origin-main sets closed:1); the 🧮 Origin launcher raises it.

metadata.name: frame
metadata.description: the 元 window's self-mounting gen-2 frame (replaces the sheetView render of 元 + win.geom).

metadata.name: cels
metadata.description: genesis: worksheets of editable cels, each like 元. TOP-LEVEL ONLY — a genesis builds the sheet; it is never a child of dom()/canvas() (nested it stringifies to "[object Object]" and never materializes). cels(rows, cols) makes one sheet (auto-named g<r>x<c>); cels(rows, cols, "name") names it; cels("in", 4, 3, "out", 4, 3) makes a WORKBOOK; cels("in", 4, 3, at("a1", "apple"), at("b2", "cel(\"monkey\")")) fills cells with initial values/formulas. To chart a grid, put the chart in a cell OF that grid: at("A5", '=canvas(360,200, barchart(sales!A2:A4, sales!B2:B4))'). delete the formula -> swept.

metadata.name: at
metadata.description: at(addr, content) - one cell's initial content for a cels() grid, e.g. cels("in", 4, 3, at("a1", "apple")).

metadata.name: geom
metadata.description: geom(x, y, w, h [, minW, minH]) - a cels() grid's WINDOW geometry, CSS-style: x/y = left/top, w/h = the (proportional) width/height, minW/minH = min-width/min-height FLOORS the window never renders or resizes below (like CSS width:50%; min-width:340px). A value in (0,1] is a PROPORTION of the viewport (→ viewport.w/.h); >1 is absolute pixels. e.g. cels("app", 4, 4, geom(0.1, 0.1, 0.5, 0.4, 340, 200), at("a1", …)). Written into win.geom[name] the first time the window materializes; a later user drag/resize is preserved.

metadata.name: doc
metadata.description: DEPRECATED legacy alias of seg/甲. genesis: compose a whole document from cels()/def()/cel() parts in one formula, e.g. doc(cels("in",2,2,at("a1","x")), def("f","js","x=>x")). What seed() emits — paste it into 元 to recreate an app.

metadata.name: seed
metadata.description: () - serialize the WHOLE document to a single recreating formula (a doc(...) / cels(...) you can paste into 元). Callable from any cel; its value becomes the seed source.

metadata.name: export
metadata.description: (segment?, form?) - serialize a document segment (or, with no arg, the WHOLE document stack); the boot substrate is never included. form "archive" (default) = a lossless 甲骨 json string for =import(); form "formula" = the re-minting formula (=cels(...)/=def(...)) for a workbook/function segment. Whole-doc formula is also =seed()/=link().

metadata.name: import
metadata.description: (src) - load an archive json string (or a =formula) into the document stack: ADD a new segment, or wholesale-REPLACE a same-named one. Refuses a boot-set name (net/dom/origin/…). =import("{...}")

metadata.name: origin.run
metadata.description: (state, cellKey) - set the cell's content from the draft and re-evaluate; rebuild the cell list (new grids in, swept out); 元 un-deletable (empty restores readme).

metadata.name: origin.edit
metadata.description: (state, cellKeyOrForceSpec) - start INLINE editing a cell (seed draft with its source); the Excel double-click path (single-click SELECTS via origin.select). Payload is the cell key, or { key, force: true } to start editing past the form-control guard.

metadata.name: origin.select
metadata.description: (state, cellKey, event) - SELECT a cell (Excel single-click): set 元.selected + 元.selectedSrc + seed 元.draft from its source, WITHOUT swapping it to the inline editor, so the grid keeps showing the value while the formula bar shows the source. A click on a form control a formula rendered is left alone.

metadata.name: origin.fire
metadata.description: (state, cellKey?) - FIRE (re-evaluate) the selected cell (or the given key): a FormulaCel re-applies its source via setValue (recompile + re-cascade); a ValueCel re-writes its own value (re-cascades dependents). Wired to the 🔫 button on the formula bar.

metadata.name: ex
metadata.description: (formula, target) - a try-it payload pairing an example formula with the cell key it should run in. Used inside the readme's yellow-lightning buttons: (on "click" "tryexample" (ex "=cels(8, 5)" "readme.B2")). Returns a marker the painter hands to tryexample verbatim as the click payload.

metadata.name: tryexample
metadata.description: (state, exPayload) - the readme 'try it' handler. Clicking a yellow ⚡ next to an example copies that example's formula into a scratch cell beside the readme (its B-column target) and evaluates it, so the result appears. Implemented by seeding 元.draft with the formula then running origin.run on the target cell, which sniffs the source into a FormulaCel, writes it, re-evaluates, and repaints.

metadata.name: origin.key
metadata.description: (state, cellKey, event) - Enter commits the draft.

metadata.name: origin.effects
metadata.description: load/cels requests commit here (effects at drain).

metadata.name: origin.drain
metadata.description: (items) - execute cels (segment listing) requests; result text replaces the request as the cel's value.

metadata.name: members
metadata.description: (segment) - readable listing of a segment's cels (skill first; locked marked).

metadata.name: inspect
metadata.description: (key) - the cel's full definition (celType, value, formula, metadata) as readable JSON.

metadata.name: segments
metadata.description: () - every loaded segment with role, version, dependencies.

metadata.name: origin.install
metadata.description: (state, archive) - persist an origin-application segment ARCHIVE (dumpSegments shape {segments,manifests}, object or JSON string) into the OPFS segment-store via store.putRaw WITHOUT loading it into state. Idempotent at name granularity (an already-stored app is skipped). The ONLY way the archive's cels reach state is a later origin.launch (hydrate-closure); install never hydrates. Returns a status string. (Distinct from winapps' app.install, which fetches asset FILES.)

metadata.name: installBakedApps
metadata.description: (state, manifest?) - first-run install of the baked APPLICATION + document segments: read the inert #plastron-apps manifest the bundle baked into the page (a { name: archive } map) and app.install each entry (OPFS only, never state). Pass `manifest` to bypass the DOM read (tests/headless). No-op off-DOM or without a filesystem. A broken baked app is logged, not thrown.

metadata.name: origin.launch
metadata.description: (state, app) - open an installed origin-application by name: hydrate its segment closure from the store (idempotent), then run its conventional ENTRY cel `<app>.entry` so it materializes its window(s). The navbar/icon click path. The app must already be installed (boot.run installs the baked set).

metadata.name: boot.run
metadata.description: (state, opts?) - the origin-application boot sequence: install every baked app archive into the store (OPFS, not state), then launch the desktop shell. Tests pass {manifest, open} to drive it headlessly; open:false installs only.

metadata.name: taskbarBar
metadata.description: (active, ...states) - render the desktop bottom taskbar: one chip per non-closed, non-docked window, the active one bordered, a minimized one dimmed. Receives each window's state VALUE; click → desktop.taskClick. Built reactively by desktop.taskbarGenesis.

metadata.name: desktop.taskbarGenesis
metadata.description: (list, active) - re-derive the taskbar from win.list. A FormulaCel (desktop.taskbarGenesis win.list win.active) re-fires when the window set or focus changes and returns a genesis whose desktop.taskbar.frame splices in each window's state cel by name, so the bar tracks min/raise/title reactively.

metadata.name: desktop.taskClick
metadata.description: (state, ref) - click a taskbar chip: a minimized window restores (clear min + raise); the active one minimizes; any other open one raises.

metadata.name: desktop.graphbtn
metadata.description: () - the round lower-left desktop button that opens the state force-graph (dispatches desktop.stategraph).

metadata.name: desktop.stategraph
metadata.description: (state) - open a force-graph of the whole state in a real window-segment window (drag/resize/minimize/fullscreen/close via wframe): one node per segment, sized by how much memory it uses, origin-application segments tinted distinctly. Reuses the forcegraph segment (fg.set + fgview).

metadata.name: origin.celtopo
metadata.description: (state, key?) - open the runCycle dependency CONE of a cel (defaults to the selected cell) as a force-graph window: upstream deps (blue) it depends on + downstream dependents (green) that depend on it + the cel itself pinned (gold), edges = inputMap propagation arrows. The 🔗 button on the formula bar dispatches it; clicking a node re-centers. Reuses the forcegraph segment (fg.set + fgview).

metadata.name: desktop.graphNode
metadata.description: (state, seg) - click a state-graph node: open that segment in the app editor (origin.editapp) to edit its cels' sources.

metadata.name: desktop.bg
metadata.description: (src, fallback) - the desktop wallpaper image. img() hydrates a /path src to an objectURL via file-store, so src can be an OPFS path or a data-URI; fallback covers an empty wallpaper. Right-click opens display settings (desktop.bgmenu).

metadata.name: desktop.bgmenu
metadata.description: (state) - right-click the wallpaper: refresh the /wallpapers/ image list and open (or raise) the display-settings window.

metadata.name: desktop.settingsView
metadata.description: (current, files) - the display-settings window body: a wallpaper preview, a file-IO import button, and a chip per image under /wallpapers/ (click → desktop.setWallpaper).

metadata.name: desktop.refreshWallpapers
metadata.description: (state) - list /wallpapers/ into the desktop.wallpapers cel (the settings grid references it, so it updates reactively). Creates the folder if missing.

metadata.name: desktop.setWallpaper
metadata.description: (state, path) - point the desktop.wallpaper cel at an OPFS path; the bg img + painter load it. Reactive repaint.

metadata.name: desktop.importWallpaper
metadata.description: (state, _, event) - file-IO import: read the picked File, write it under /wallpapers/, then select it as the wallpaper. Browser-only (File API).

metadata.name: desktop.icons
metadata.description: (iconpos, mobile, ...items) - desktop: free-positioned, draggable app icons (positions persisted in desktop.iconpos by label); mobile: today's collapsible nav. items are item(label, action); a click LAUNCHES via origin.navOpen.

metadata.name: desktop.iconGrab
metadata.description: (state, label, event) - pointerdown on a desktop icon: capture the pointer + record the grab offset in desktop.icondrag.

metadata.name: desktop.iconMove
metadata.description: (state, _, event) - pointermove while dragging an icon: update desktop.iconpos[label] to the pointer position; repaint.

metadata.name: desktop.iconDrop
metadata.description: (state) - pointerup: record how far the icon moved (desktop.iconLastMoved, so a drag suppresses the click) and clear desktop.icondrag.

metadata.name: desktop.iconClick
metadata.description: (state, action) - launch the icon's app via origin.navOpen UNLESS the pointer dragged (a drag is not a click).

metadata.name: sheetcells
metadata.description: (keys, vals) - zip a key list + value list into sheetgrid entries {key,col,row,value}, deriving col/row from each key's A1 suffix. The host formula passes the keys (strings) + the cel values (a list referencing each cel, so the grid is reactive).

metadata.name: origin.editapp
metadata.description: (state, app) - open another segment's cels as an editable source list (its formulas/definition): each cel as key → editable source; Enter commits. Click a node in the state force-graph to edit that segment. sheetapp-as-editor.

metadata.name: origin.editAppCel
metadata.description: (state, {app,key}, event) - commit an edited cel source from the app editor (on Enter): rewrite the cel's source, then refresh the editor.

metadata.name: origin.savedoc
metadata.description: (state, name) - record the document's cel states: saveUserSpace dehydrates the origin-user segment's private closure and store.put's it under the app's documents/ subfolder.

metadata.name: vocab
metadata.description: (segment?) - the values + functions usable in formulas (callable lambdas/compilers + value cels) with descriptions; no arg = across all loaded segments.

metadata.name: viewport
metadata.description: () - current page metrics {w, h, mobile, orient} as a one-shot snapshot. For REACTIVE layout reference the cels instead: viewport.w / viewport.h / viewport.mobile / viewport.orient update on window resize, so a formula re-runs to relayout — =IF(viewport.mobile, dom("h1","phone"), win("app","App",body)) or =win("app","App",body, viewport.w, viewport.h - 40).

metadata.name: viewportSync
metadata.description: (host) writes live page metrics into the viewport.* cels so formulas that reference them re-run; the host calls it at boot and on resize.

metadata.name: clockSync
metadata.description: (host) writes the current time into the clock (HH:MM) + clock.full cels so a formula referencing them (e.g. a taskbar) re-renders; the host calls it on an interval. Reference `clock` in a formula instead of a banned NOW().

metadata.name: item
metadata.description: (label, action, ...children) - one navigation menu node for nav(). label is text/emoji; action is a window KEY (clicking focuses that window) or a '=formula' (clicking spawns a new window running it), or omit action for a pure submenu parent. children are more item()s (WordPress-style nesting). e.g. item("📊 Charts", item("🥧 Pie", '=cels(3,2, ...piechart...)')).

metadata.name: nav
metadata.description: ([mobile], ...items) - a navigation menu from item() nodes. Pass viewport.mobile as the first arg so it AUTO-SWITCHES: a collapsible left sidebar (☰) on mobile, desktop icon-launchers otherwise (it re-renders on rotate/resize). Nesting collapses via native <details>. e.g. =nav(viewport.mobile, item("📁 Files","files"), item("📊 Charts", item("🥧 Pie", '=cels(3,2,at("A1","x"))'))).

metadata.name: navOpen
metadata.description: dispatch target for a clicked nav leaf: a '=formula' action spawns a new window (trusted, capped by the kernel); any other action is a window key and focuses that window.

metadata.name: def
metadata.description: (name, kind, source) - define a callable function from source in a compiler kind ("js" works out of the box). =def("double", "js", "x => x * 2") then call it: =double(21) -> 42.

metadata.name: cdn
metadata.description: (url) - load an external script/library from a URL via the kernel loadScript primitive. =cdn("https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/canvas-confetti") then call what it exposes.

metadata.name: ls
metadata.description: (path?) - list a directory in OPFS (default /). dirs show a trailing /.

metadata.name: tree
metadata.description: (path?) - recursive directory tree in OPFS (default /).

metadata.name: mkdir
metadata.description: (path) - make a directory in OPFS (recursive).

metadata.name: rm
metadata.description: (path) - remove a file or directory from OPFS (auto file-vs-dir).

metadata.name: mv
metadata.description: (from, to) - move/rename a file or directory in OPFS.

metadata.name: cat
metadata.description: (path) - read a text file from OPFS into the cell.

metadata.name: write
metadata.description: (path, text) - write text to a file in OPFS (create/overwrite).

metadata.name: touch
metadata.description: (path) - create an empty file in OPFS if it does not exist.

metadata.name: stat
metadata.description: (path) - size / isDir / mtime of an OPFS path.

metadata.name: hash
metadata.description: (seg, ...exclude) - a recent SHA-256 (hex) of worksheet `seg`s SOURCE cels (ValueCel value | FormulaCel formula-text; derived values excluded - sources only, so it is deterministic across replicas). Trailing-* exclude patterns drop ephemeral/IO ranges. =hash("budget") / =hash("budget", "budget.live*").

metadata.name: segs
metadata.description: () - list sheets saved to OPFS (=saveSeg/openSeg/delSeg manage them).

metadata.name: saveSeg
metadata.description: (name) - save the whole current sheet to an OPFS file under /plastron/sheets.

metadata.name: openSeg
metadata.description: (name) - restore a sheet previously saved with saveSeg from OPFS.

metadata.name: delSeg
metadata.description: (name) - delete a saved sheet from OPFS.

metadata.name: downloadSeg
metadata.description: (name) - a button that downloads a saved sheet (.json) from OPFS.

metadata.name: db
metadata.description: (name?) - open/create a sqlite database in OPFS (default main). returns a handle for sql()/tables().

metadata.name: sql
metadata.description: (db, query) - run SQL against a db handle; SELECT returns rows, writes persist to OPFS.

metadata.name: tables
metadata.description: (db) - list the tables in a db.

metadata.name: dbseed
metadata.description: (db, rows, table) - bulk-load a JSON array of row objects into a table. e.g. =dbseed(mydb, A1:C9, "turtles")

metadata.name: schema
metadata.description: (db) - introspect the database: tables, columns, primary keys and foreign keys (the basis for the visual query builder).

metadata.name: dbexport
metadata.description: (db, path) - serialize the database to a portable .db blob and write it to a file-store path (browsable / downloadable). e.g. =dbexport(mydb, "/exports/mydb.db")

metadata.name: dbimport
metadata.description: (db, path) - load a .db file from a file-store path INTO the database, replacing its contents. e.g. =dbimport(mydb, "/exports/mydb.db")

metadata.name: interlinked
metadata.description: (seg) - force-directed graph of a grid segment's cels (nodes) + their inputMap deps (edges), drawn on canvas.

metadata.name: simulate
metadata.description: (fnName, n?) - def-driven animation: run a def'd frame fn (i -> [x, y]) n times and play the trajectory on an animated canvas.

metadata.name: save
metadata.description: (name?) - persist your sheet (cell sources + def'd functions) to this browser's localStorage. =save() then reload and it's back; =save("v2") for a named slot.

metadata.name: open
metadata.description: (name?) - restore a saved sheet from localStorage. =open() loads the default slot; =open("v2") a named one.

metadata.name: link
metadata.description: (target?, base?) - a shareable URL that rebuilds a plastron from the page address (#f= hash, deflate+base64url). =link() encodes the WHOLE sheet; =link("元") encodes one cell's source; =link("", "") makes a relative #f= that works from a file. Paste the URL anywhere — it survives a tweet (t.co shortens it).

metadata.name: unlink
metadata.description: (url) - decode a =link() URL (or bare #f= payload) back to its formula source, as text. The inverse of link. Does NOT run it — paste the source into a cell yourself.

metadata.name: encrypt
metadata.description: (passphrase?, target?, base?) - like link, but AES-256-GCM the source behind a passphrase. The URL parameter names the method: https://plastron.ca/#aes256gcm=<ciphertext>. =encrypt() encrypts the WHOLE sheet; =encrypt("", "元") one cell. Omit the passphrase to be PROMPTED (so it never lands in the sheet). Pipeline: deflate → AES-256-GCM (PBKDF2-SHA256, 600k) → base64url; AES-256 is quantum-resistant. The URL is opaque; share the passphrase out-of-band. Caveat: the decrypted formula lives in browser memory — run a local index.html offline for high stakes.

metadata.name: decrypt
metadata.description: (url, passphrase?) - decode a =encrypt() URL (or bare #aes256gcm= payload) back to its formula source, as text. The inverse of encrypt. Omit the passphrase to be PROMPTED. Does NOT run it — paste the source into a cell yourself. A wrong passphrase or tampered link yields an error (GCM authenticates).

metadata.name: otpEncrypt
metadata.description: (target?) - ONE-TIME-PAD encrypt with UNCONDITIONAL secrecy (perfect, quantum-immune). Renders a file picker: choose a pad file of random bytes (≥ message length + 32) shared with your peer. Produces https://plastron.ca/#otp=<padName>.<ciphertext> — ciphertext = formula XOR pad, plus a one-time Carter-Wegman MAC for unconditional integrity. NO compression (would leak length info). One pad file = ONE message: DELETE it from both stacks after use; never reuse a pad. target "" = whole sheet; a cell key = its source.

metadata.name: otpDecrypt
metadata.description: (url) - decode a =otpEncrypt() #otp= link. Renders a file picker for the matching pad (the URL names which pad). Returns the formula source as text in the formula bar; does NOT run it. A wrong pad or tampered message fails the MAC check. Delete the pad after use.

metadata.name: otpLoader
metadata.description: (padId, payload) - the boot view a #otp= URL renders as 元: a file picker to load the named pad and decrypt the shared plastron (kernel stays LOCKED). Used by bootFromHash; not usually called by hand.

metadata.name: origin.otpEncrypt
metadata.description: (state, target, event) - dispatch target: XOR the source with the picked pad → an #otp= URL in the formula bar; warns to delete the spent pad.

metadata.name: origin.otpDecrypt
metadata.description: (state, url, event) - dispatch target: decrypt an #otp= payload with the picked pad → the formula source in the formula bar (does not run it).

metadata.name: origin.otpUnlock
metadata.description: (state, payload, event) - boot dispatch target: load the pad → decrypt → the shared formula becomes 元 (still jailed/locked).

metadata.name: kernel
metadata.description: (seed, preset?) - spawn a QUARANTINED child plastron from a seed formula in a fresh segment (app1, app2, …). preset = locked (default) | compute | net | trusted, capped by THIS kernel's trust. The child's cells live under <seg>.*; gated capabilities (code/net/storage) come back #DENIED unless the preset grants them. A #f= share URL is just a locked seed.

metadata.name: jail
metadata.description: (seed) - render a SANDBOXED iframe running the seed formula as its OWN kernel. allow-scripts but no allow-same-origin → opaque origin: it cannot touch localStorage, the parent page, or other tabs. The browser's real Layer-A jail for untrusted plastrons.

metadata.name: jailask
metadata.description: (payload) - JAIL ONLY: round-trip a request to the PARENT over the postMessage bridge and return its reply. The jail has no keys/network of its own; the parent mediates (e.g. an LLM call). Outside a jail it is a no-op.

metadata.name: origin.savepage
metadata.description: (state) - download the running plastron as a single self-contained 龜甲.html you can re-open or redeploy anywhere. Wired to the ⬇ 龜甲 button in the desktop's upper-right corner.

metadata.name: origin.tone
metadata.description: (state, freq) - play ONE Web Audio oscillator note at the given frequency (Hz). Loads the sound segment on first use. Wire it to a button: (on "click" "origin.tone" 440).

metadata.name: origin.music
metadata.description: (state) - play a short melody (Ode to Joy) via the Web Audio sound segment. Browser audio is autoplay-gated, so trigger it from a click.

metadata.name: origin.compose
metadata.description: (state) - start 'Symphony of Cels', an ORIGINAL generative phase piece (pentatonic voices at incommensurate periods, evolving harmony). Web Audio autoplay-gated → start from a click. origin.composeStop ends it.

metadata.name: origin.composeStop
metadata.description: (state) - stop the generative piece started by origin.compose.

metadata.name: origin.playmelody
metadata.description: (state, seg) - read column A of sheet seg as a RANGE of note frequencies (Hz) and play them in sequence. Type numbers down a column to write a tune; wire a button: on("click","origin.playmelody","melody").

metadata.name: origin.tile
metadata.description: (state, segs?) - auto-layout worksheet windows: size each to its CONTENT (capped to the viewport) and PACK them non-overlapping instead of stacked. segs = a list/comma-string, or all open windows.

metadata.name: origin.autoload
metadata.description: (state) - restore the default saved sheet on boot; the host calls this after hydrate.

metadata.name: origin.seedWallpaper
metadata.description: (state) - write the shipped wallpaper (windows.wallpaper data-URI) into an OPFS file at /desktop/wallpaper.<ext> and point desktop.A2 at it, so the desktop background LOADS FROM A FILE in OPFS, not a hard-coded constant. Idempotent; preserves a user-set wallpaper path. Host-called once after boot.

metadata.name: origin.seedIndexHtml
metadata.description: (state) - seed the page's OWN served HTML (document.documentElement.outerHTML) into OPFS at /plastron/index.html so the file explorer isn't empty — it shows 'the index.html that plastron makes'. Best-effort; no-op off-DOM or when the file-store backend is none. Host-called once after boot. NOTE: only OPFS contents are reachable from the browser sandbox — the full repo tree is not.

metadata.name: view.refresh
metadata.description: host hook called by settleStructural after out-of-band structure materializes — rebuilds 元.cells + repaints

metadata.name: mount
metadata.description: (target content) - pin a dom under another element of the sheet instead of in the cell that holds it. target is a selector matched against the view: ".sheet" pins under the cells, "div.cell" under the first cell, "#id" by id; a bare word ("top"/"bottom") is a region anchor laid out around the sheet. Deleting the formula removes it.

metadata.name: viewfire
metadata.description: (vals) - the gen-2 desktop compositor behind 元.view (replaces sheetView): vals is the cell values of every whitelisted self-mounting frame (cellKeys); look each up in the mount registry and splice the windows into the positioned .origin desktop, mounted at #app. Renders nothing of its own.

Desktop layout argument: "rowflow" (default) lays WIDE windows in rows that wrap and overflow downward; "masonry" packs them into narrow screen-width columns; "free" leaves them. 元 leads top-left. Set visibly via segment("rowflow"|"masonry"|"free", ...).

metadata.name: win.geom
metadata.description: per-window geometry (x/y/w/h/z) and tab relationships (host) keyed by sheet segment. readme is seeded BIG and roughly centered (x 300, y 90, w 860, h 680) so the welcome card lands front-and-centre; chat/turtlecharts carry only host so they tab into clients/turtles.

metadata.name: segment
metadata.description: genesis: compose a SEGMENT (document) from cels()/winapp()/chatapp()/def()/cel() parts in one formula, e.g. =segment(...). (was doc.)
